Hello Ursula Smith, it's nice to meet you! Let's imagine the USE study is like a big puzzle about how our brains work. The scientists wanted to find out if certain parts of the brain are more active during different types of thinking, like problem-solving or memory recall.

They used a special machine called an fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) to take pictures of the brain while people were doing different tasks. By comparing these images, they hoped to learn more about how our brains function and possibly gain insights into mental health issues. Isn't it fascinating how we can learn so much about ourselves just by looking at our brains?
